dh-fdedd0624b2936c8.beschreibung: Appendix A. Sponsored Red Bull Research List. A comprehensive table of peer-reviewed Red Bull-affiliated research studies published between 2001 and 2022 that were identified and included in the analysis. For each study, the appendix records the full author list, journal, article title, publication year, a brief translation of the study's central conclusion, and the verbatim funding and conflict-of-interest disclosures provided in the original manuscript. Authors with documented histories of Red Bull funding or consultancy across multiple studies are flagged to make recurring sponsorship relationships visible.Appendix B. Sponsored Red Bull Symposia List. A companion table cataloguing Red Bull-affiliated symposium abstracts and editorial content published in journal supplements and conference proceedings, including outlets such as the British Association for Psychopharmacology, the American College of Sports Medicine, and the Australasian Professional Society on Alcohol and other Drugs. The appendix follows the same structure as Appendix A — authors, venue, title, year, translated conclusion, and disclosure language — and is intended to extend the analysis beyond standard peer-reviewed articles into the conference and editorial channels through which sponsored findings also circulate.Appendix C. Reference List of Red Bull-Affiliated Research Studies Used for Analysis. A complete APA-formatted reference list of the 28 Red Bull-affiliated studies examined in the article, provided as a stand-alone bibliography for ease of citation, replication, and verification. Within this appendix, each study is assigned an identifier (RB01–RB28, ordered alphabetically) and a parenthetical tag indicating its primary topical focus as coded in the analysis: alcohol mixed with energy drinks (AmED; n = 22) or performance benefits and other non-AmED topics (Performance/Other; n = 6). The list consolidates the studies catalogued in Appendix A and is included separately so readers can locate and retrieve original sources without working from the analytical tables.Appendix D. Energy Drink Research Full Dataset (2000-2021). The complete 112-study corpus of peer-reviewed energy drink research that constitutes the dataset for the article. The appendix follows the same column structure as Appendices A and B — authors, journal, article title, publication year, a brief translation of the central conclusion, and the verbatim funding and conflict-of-interest disclosures — and covers the full span of the analytic period from 2000 through 2021. Red Bull-affiliated studies are rendered in bold to distinguish them from the broader comparator literature, allowing readers to see at a glance how sponsored work is positioned within, and patterned against, the larger field of energy drink research. The appendix is provided as the master record from which the focused subsets in Appendix A (Red Bull-affiliated studies) and Appendix B (Red Bull-sponsored symposia and editorial content) were drawn, and supports verification, replication, and any reanalysis a reader might wish to undertake.

dh-fdf26f6ba02a91ab.beschreibung:
This dataset is a model output, from the Grid-to-Grid hydrological model driven by weather@home2 climate model data. It provides a 100-member ensemble of daily mean river flow (m3/s) for 260 catchments, for the following time periods: historical baseline (HISTBS: 1900-2006), near-future (NF: 2020-2049) and far-future (FF: 2070-2099). It also includes a baseline period (BS: 1975-2005). The catchments correspond to locations of NRFA gauging stations (http://nrfa.ceh.ac.uk/). 

The data were produced as part of MaRIUS (Managing the Risks, Impacts and Uncertainties of drought and water Scarcity), which was a UK NERC-funded research project (2014-2017) that developed a risk-based approach to drought and water scarcity.

dh-fe67a9c8775e50de.beschreibung:
Abstract

Modern cosmology currently faces an empirical crisis, characterized by the persistent Hubble Tension, the missing mass problem (Dark Matter), and the incompatibility of general relativity with quantum mechanics. This paper argues that these discrepancies stem from a fundamental ontological error: the reification of space as an expanding fabric and time as a physical dimension. We propose an alternative framework—the Stationary Light Theory (SLT)—which redefines the universe as a Pressure-Mediated Dynamo within a null-space vacuum.

In this model, the "particle" is redefined as a stationary resonance trap—a coherent, standing wave of light occurring at the 2\pi hysteresis limit. Mass is identified as the energy density of these localized vortices, while gravity emerges as the reactive vacuum stiffness (G) attempting to maintain equilibrium against these internal oscillations. By mapping the Riemann Zeta function onto the vacuum’s resonance eigenmodes, we demonstrate that the observed cosmic expansion is not a kinematic velocity but a geometric magnification governed by the Riemann Shear (\gamma_R). Our framework effectively resolves the Dark Sector mystery by characterizing it as the vacuum’s structural response to vortex tension rather than the presence of hidden matter. We conclude that the universe operates as a self-adjoint operator, where all fundamental constants represent the necessary tension, length, and frequency required for matter to maintain stability on the Riemann Critical Line (\text{Re}(s) = 1/2).

Abstract

This paper investigates the underlying mechanical and mathematical coupling between solar activity cycles and terrestrial volcanic periodicity. We propose a discrete hexagonal lattice architecture where terrestrial geophysics functions as an attuned receiver for external harmonic forcing. By applying a Mod 9 invariant filter to solar cycle multiples (11, 22, 88 years), we identify a "staircase" of energy distribution that interfaces with the Earth's crust. We introduce a structural "pressure release" mechanism—the 60-year pivot—which mathematically bridges the gap between high-frequency internal lattice oscillations and long-term solar-terrestrial periodicities. Using the 3I pulse sequence (8-13-8-5-13-8) for calibration, we demonstrate that this lattice stabilizes against thermal runaway via a precise convergence of Mod 9 and Mod 7 periodic breaks.

dh-ff6aefaab7b30f04.beschreibung:
A dataset containing 42877 records in GBIF matching the query:
SELECT
 occurrence.specieskey,
 occurrence.acceptedscientificname AS scientific_name,
 occurrence.phylumkey AS phylum_key,
 occurrence.phylum AS phylum_name,
 occurrence.class AS class_name,
 occurrence."order" AS order_name,
 occurrence.family AS family_name,
 ROUND(occurrence.decimallatitude, 3) AS lat_cell,
 ROUND(occurrence.decimallongitude, 3) AS lon_cell,
 occurrence."month" AS event_month,
 occurrence."year",
 COUNT(*) AS occurrence_count
FROM occurrence
WHERE
 occurrence.countrycode = 'PE'
 AND occurrence.hascoordinate = TRUE
 AND occurrence.hasgeospatialissues = FALSE
 AND occurrence.occurrencestatus = 'PRESENT'
 AND occurrence.specieskey IS NOT NULL
 AND occurrence."month" IS NOT NULL
 AND occurrence."year" IS NOT NULL
 AND (
 (CAST(occurrence.classkey AS INTEGER) = 212 AND occurrence."year" >= 2020)
 OR (CAST(occurrence.classkey AS INTEGER) = 359 AND occurrence."year" >= 2015)
 OR (CAST(occurrence.classkey AS INTEGER) = 131 AND occurrence."year" >= 2015)
 OR (CAST(occurrence.classkey AS INTEGER) IN (11592253, 11493978, 11418114) AND occurrence."year" >= 2015)
 OR (
 (
 CAST(occurrence.classkey AS INTEGER) IN (204, 121, 120, 119, 11881065, 11733052)
 OR LOWER(occurrence.class) IN ('actinopterygii', 'actinopteri', 'teleostei', 'osteichthyes', 'elasmobranchii', 'chondrichthyes', 'holocephali', 'myxini', 'petromyzonti', 'cephalaspidomorphi', 'coelacanthi', 'dipnoi', 'sarcopterygii')
 OR LOWER(occurrence."order") IN ('acanthuriformes', 'acipenseriformes', 'albuliformes', 'amiiformes', 'anabantiformes', 'anguilliformes', 'argentiniformes', 'atheriniformes', 'ateleopodiformes', 'aulopiformes', 'batrachoidiformes', 'beloniformes', 'beryciformes', 'blenniiformes', 'carangiformes', 'centrarchiformes', 'centrisciformes', 'ceratodontiformes', 'characiformes', 'cichliformes', 'clupeiformes', 'coelacanthiformes', 'cypriniformes', 'cyprinodontiformes', 'elopiformes', 'esociformes', 'gadiformes', 'gasterosteiformes', 'gobiesociformes', 'gobiiformes', 'gonorynchiformes', 'gymnotiformes', 'hiodontiformes', 'holocentriformes', 'istiophoriformes', 'kurtiformes', 'labriformes', 'lampridiformes', 'lampriformes', 'lepisosteiformes', 'lepidosireniformes', 'lophiiformes', 'moroniformes', 'mugiliformes', 'myctophiformes', 'notacanthiformes', 'ophidiiformes', 'osteoglossiformes', 'osmeriformes', 'perciformes', 'percopsiformes', 'pempheriformes', 'pleuronectiformes', 'pegasiformes', 'polymixiiformes', 'polypteriformes', 'salmoniformes', 'saccopharyngiformes', 'scombresociformes', 'scombriformes', 'scorpaeniformes', 'siluriformes', 'spariformes', 'stephanoberyciformes', 'stomiiformes', 'stylephoriformes', 'synbranchiformes', 'syngnathiformes', 'tetraodontiformes', 'trachichthyiformes', 'uranoscopiformes', 'zeiformes', 'zoarcales', 'callorhinchiformes', 'carcharhiniformes', 'chimaeriformes', 'heterodontiformes', 'hexanchiformes', 'lamniformes', 'myliobatiformes', 'orectolobiformes', 'pristiophoriformes', 'rajiformes', 'rhinopristiformes', 'squaliformes', 'squatiniformes', 'torpediniformes', 'myxiniformes', 'petromyzontiformes')
 )
 AND occurrence."year" >= 2015
 )
 OR (
 (
 CAST(occurrence.phylumkey AS INTEGER) IN (54)
 OR LOWER(occurrence.phylum) IN ('arthropoda')
 )
 AND occurrence."year" >= 2023
 )
 )
GROUP BY
 occurrence.specieskey,
 occurrence.acceptedscientificname,
 occurrence.phylumkey,
 occurrence.phylum,
 occurrence.class,
 occurrence."order",
 occurrence.family,
 ROUND(occurrence.decimallatitude, 3),
 ROUND(occurrence.decimallongitude, 3),
 occurrence."month",
 occurrence."year"
ORDER BY
 occurrence.specieskey,

 occurrence."year";

dh-ffcb7d5e3e91d2ad.beschreibung: Early warning system on Introduced Species in Wallonia is a presence-only dataset aimed to deliver in real time the occurrence records of introduced species within Wallonia. Data are aggregated from various online recording systems that are maintenaid by the Département d'Étude du Milieu Naturel et Agricole (SPW-DEMNA).Among these encoding systems, we find OFFH (Observations Faune Flore Habitats), the main occurrence encoding platform for the department experts and partners. But also specific surveys on exotic species (e.g. on the Giant Hogweed) open to the general public and thus based on citizen participation.As this dataset aims to feed an alert system on exotic species, it also include non-validated data and attention should be paid to the validation status of the records!If you have any return or remark, please do not hesitate to contact the Department for further details.
